name: ApexSim Engine
problem: Discrete event simulation frameworks in interpreted languages suffer from massive garbage collection overhead and lack precise deterministic priority queue coordination for millions of concurrent events.
pain: Debugging complex multi-agent or hardware simulation timelines is slow when event queues bottleneck on locking overhead and lack fine-grained causality tracing.
solution: A zero-dependency discrete event simulation (DES) engine written in Java 21 featuring a lock-free calendar queue, a custom domain-specific simulation scripting parser, time-dilation stepping, and automated causality violation detection.
verification: Unit test suite simulating one million ordered events with injected random out-of-order scheduling attempts, verifying that causality violations throw immediate runtime exceptions and state replays match byte-for-byte.
major_features: Custom calendar queue priority scheduler implementing O(1) expected-time event insertions and extractions
Domain-Specific Language (DSL) lexer and parser for defining simulation actor states and transition triggers
Virtual Thread-based parallel event dispatcher executing independent simulation steps concurrently
Causality tracking engine validating happened-before temporal constraints across asynchronous actor nodes
State-snapshotting checkpoint manager supporting time-travel debugging and forward-backward stepping
Deterministic pseudorandom number generator (PRNG) stream interleaving for reproducible stochastic runs
Append-only binary audit log recording every event execution path with CRC32 integrity validation
Real-time performance metrics collector monitoring event throughput, queue depth, and memory allocation rates
truth_policy: Only validated behavior may be claimed as working.
